messages.author: 5db21e7785ef2433
messages.subject: UnmarkedFrameDSO nonparboot error
parts:
Hi all,

I am working on data collected during aerial survey, from 1997 to 2004. 
First, I used UnmarkedFrameDSO function on my data and then use distsampOpen to add the effect of my variables which looks like that:
#-------------------------------
m4 <-
  distsampOpen(
    lambdaformula = ~vege + ele,
    gammaformula = ~year, 
    omegaformula = ~year, 
    pformula = ~ele, 
    data = unm_Graz_apr,
    keyfun = "halfnorm", 
    output = "abund",
    unitsOut = "kmsq",
    K= 100)
#------------------------------
Now, I would like to look at the estimation of the abundance each year and use bootstrapping to estimate the standard error. However, when I ran this: 

npb <- nonparboot(m4, B=10) # I have an error
Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :
  non-finite finite-difference value [4]

So, I tried to decrease B which was already very (too) small and it worked (B = 3). But then I have another error:

smoothed(npb)[2,]))
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘smoothed’ for signature ‘"unmarkedFitDSO"’

Same error if I do:
smoothed(m4)
Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  : 
  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘smoothed’ for signature ‘"unmarkedFitDSO"’

Obviously, I am doing something wrong here but I can't figure it out what. 
Thank you for your help.

Anne

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] UnmarkedFrameDSO nonparboot error
parts:
Hi Anne,

If your dataset is relatively small (in terms of sites) and/or sparse, resampling the existing sites can easily result in new datasets which unmarked has problems fitting, especially considering this relatively complex model. So the higher the B the more chance you run into one of these and get an error. I believe it is possible to iteratively call nonparboot on the same model with small B to slowly build up working fits.

The smoothed function only works on dynamic occupancy models. Probably what you want for estimating abundance each year is ranef().

You may also consider fitting a "stacked" single-season model with year as a covariate if you have issues fitting the model, it's hard to get these dynamic abundance models to work.

Ken

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] UnmarkedFrameDSO nonparboot error
parts:
It looks like the problem is the value of K you set (180). This should be higher than the total count at any given site-period, which based on your data must be larger than 346 (one site-period has distance bin counts 0, 173, 173 so total count at the site 346).

This should have been caught before the model was fit and it is for me - are you perhaps using an older version of unmarked than the one on CRAN?

Ken

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] UnmarkedFrameDSO nonparboot error
parts:
Hi Ken,

Thank you for this. The codes work now. I thought that K was supposed to be higher than the highest count, not the highest one within the distance interval. This is where the problem was so thank you very much. 

Unfortunately, I am not using the latest version of unmarked as I am having difficulties to update it. Some packages are difficult (sometimes impossible) to update on Mac, which can be very frustrating. 

Anne

Le mercredi 13 décembre 2023 à 16:24:36 UTC+2, Ken Kellner a écrit :
It looks like the problem is the value of K you set (180). This should be higher than the total count at any given site-period, which based on your data must be larger than 346 (one site-period has distance bin counts 0, 173, 173 so total count at the site 346).

This should have been caught before the model was fit and it is for me - are you perhaps using an older version of unmarked than the one on CRAN?

Ken
